stories.title: Zacharia out
stories.text: On Friday, after days of intense scrutiny about her legal credentials, Zacharia was “transitioned out” of the role. CNN reported that Zacharia’s removal was a direct result of her inability to satisfactorily respond to Popular Information’s reporting, which became a problem for her even on typically friendly platforms like Fox News: After a string of surprisingly combative interviews on Fox News – specifically her appearance with Trump’s friend Sean Hannity on Thursday night, when the host grilled her over her legal credentials – the president decided it was untenable for her to remain in the role. Zacharia’s abrupt removal was a damaging development for Republicans so close to the midterm elections. “18 days until Election Day, and instead of driving this unifying message, Republicans are dealing with the fallout of Katie Zacharia’s firing after just five days on the job,” CNN’s Laura Coates said. That’s Popular Information’s mission: we investigate, uncover new facts, and hold the powerful accountable. stories.title: “Win, Lose, or Draw,” Pearson Campaign Builds a Progressive Coalition in Rural Tennessee
stories.text: Tennessee state Rep. Justin J. Pearson stands for a photo with supporters at Campbell Chapel M.B. Story by Katherine Burgess Cherie Marceaux lives in Lawrence County, about three hours from Memphis. She and her husband run an animal rescue with horses, goats, pigs, dogs, ferrets, and more. Marceaux says she’s not a Democrat or a Republican, but she knows who she wants to vote for in Tennessee’s newly redrawn 9th Congressional District: Memphis Democrat and State Rep. Justin J. Pearson. In 2023 Pearson was expelled by Republicans from the state legislature as part of a protest for tighter gun safety laws with the “Tennessee Three.” Instead of silencing his cause, the expulsion drew national attention and rallied Memphians around his leadership. When Tennessee Republicans redrew congressional district lines in May, they intended to make District 9 a safe Republican seat. In response, Pearson has focused on issues that appeal to urban and rural voters across the political spectrum: opposition to data centers, gun safety and the economy. stories.title: Why Trump Nixed Execution Livestream
stories.text: Trump responds to a reporter’s question on October 9 Fundraising fell off a cliff this summer. Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. This ignores the real story, one that’s extraordinary for several reasons. First, the decision was never Hegseth’s to make; it was the president’s alone, as I reported . Second, he initially supported it, saying so to a reporter on October 9. Third and most significantly, Trump’s reversal is the result of people power, with an overwhelming majority of Americans — including his own supporters — opposed to the grotesque spectacle worthy of ancient Rome. Yet instead of a story about ordinary Americans standing up to the most powerful leader on earth and winning , headline after headline frames it as a Washington drama, as shown below. Consciously or not, they turn what is basically a story about people power into just another Trump fuck-up. stories.title: I’ve Spent My Life Fighting Corruption. Finally America Is Going To Vote On It.
stories.text: I’ve spent most of my adult life toiling away in many different political and journalism jobs, but focused on one single mission the whole time: a mission to show that corruption isn’t an inevitability or an abstraction, but is instead a human-manufactured system that directly harms us all in concrete ways. That work across books , articles , op-eds , videos , newspaper columns , reporting projects , podcasts and films culminated in the creation of The Lever six years ago, and the release of the very first episode of our podcast series Master Plan two years ago, in which I argued: Your life is worse than it should be thanks to the corruption of American democracy. Trouble earning enough to pay your credit card bill and your rent ? You can thank the corporate donors who delivered cash to lawmakers who then blocked a minimum wage increase, blocked rent control, and blocked a cap on credit card interest rates. Are you one of the 112 million Americans who struggle to pay for health care? You can thank the health insurance companies, who funneled millions of dollars to lawmakers to make sure they keep America as the only industrialized country without government-guaranteed healthcare. stories.title: Tim Walz Warns That Democrats Can Win And Still Lose
stories.text: LISTEN NOW: With the midterms less than a month away, some pundits and polls suggest Democrats have the election in the bag. But is that really true? David Sirota travels to Minnesota to speak with someone who knows the danger of election complacency and overconfidence: Democratic Gov. Tim Walz. Today on Lever Time , we’re airing David Sirota’s full conversation with Walz. They reflect on the choices that led to a 2024 presidential defeat for the Democrats, from the party’s stance on the genocide in Gaza to Kamala Harris’s decision to campaign with Republican Liz Cheney. Ahead of the 2026 midterms, what can we learn from Walz's experience? Does he believe the Democrats stand a chance? And what happens if the Democrats win and fail to deliver on their promises?
